How to use Image Compressor

Features

  • Private browser compression

Best way to use Image Compressor

Image Compressor focuses on quick browser-side size reduction with visible before/after size feedback.

Best for

  • Reducing phone photo size before upload
  • Optimizing blog or website images
  • Creating smaller shareable images without server upload

Example workflow

Example: upload a 3MB JPG, choose WebP or JPG output, set quality around 0.80, and compare the downloaded size.

Quality notes

A moderate quality value around 0.75–0.85 is usually the best balance for photos.

Before you download

  • Check that the output format matches the website, form, or software where you will upload it.
  • Open the downloaded file once before final submission so you can confirm quality, page order, dimensions, and readability.
  • If the result is too large, use the related compression or resize tools instead of repeating the same step many times.
  • If the source file is password-protected, corrupted, scanned, or extremely large, use a desktop or specialist tool when browser processing is not enough.

Troubleshooting

  • If the result is still large, reduce dimensions with Image Resizer first.
  • PNG photos often compress better when converted to JPG or WebP.
  • Keep logos/screenshots as PNG when crisp edges matter.

Common uses for Image Compressor

  • prepare photos for forms and profiles
  • optimize website images
  • convert images for compatibility

Tips for better results

For the best balance of size and quality, start with a clear original image and choose JPG or WebP for smaller photo files.
